feature1.prompt: Inherited classes are not correctly documented when mocked. The issue manifests when documenting classes that inherit from mocked classes, where the 'Bases' section in the generated documentation shows an incomplete name (for example, 'torch.nn.' instead of 'torch.nn.Module'). The problem appears in certain versions of Sphinx (specifically for sphinx>=3.4.2) where the inherited class’s name is not properly recorded. The fix should ensure that the internal attributes representing the class name are correctly assigned so that the documentation shows the full and proper base class name.
feature1.hint_texts: This feature involves modifying the implementation of the _MockObject class in sphinx/ext/autodoc/mock.py. The changes should include initializing the __name__ attribute and updating the __qualname__ assignment in the __init__ method to utilize the new __name__ value. Furthermore, when creating subclasses via the _make_subclass function, the '__name__' attribute must be correctly set. The implementation must result in inherited mocked classes being documented with their accurate fully qualified names.
feature1.entrypoint: File: sphinx/ext/autodoc/mock.py; Modify the _MockObject class (especially the __init__ method) and the _make_subclass function to ensure proper assignment of __name__ and __qualname__.

feature2.prompt: Inherited classes that utilize mocked classes are not being properly documented, resulting in errors in the 'Bases' section of the documentation. The expected behavior is that the full name of the base class (such as 'torch.nn.Module') is displayed rather than an incomplete identifier. This improvement is critical for ensuring that the generated documentation accurately reflects class hierarchies. The solution must be verifiable by confirming that the correct base class names appear in the documentation output.
feature2.hint_texts: This feature focuses on adding test cases to validate that the fixes implemented for _MockObject correctly result in proper documentation of inherited classes. Developers should add tests in tests/test_util_typing.py that simulate the scenario with mocked classes, checking the output of functions like restify and stringify. The tests must be designed such that they initially fail before the fix and pass after the implementation, thereby confirming that the 'Bases' section is rendered accurately. It is essential to coordinate with the implementation modifications to ensure that the tests correctly capture the intended behavior.
feature2.entrypoint: File: tests/test_util_typing.py; Add new test functions, in particular test_restify_mock and test_stringify_mock, to check that mocked classes are now documented with the correct base class names.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: Both features interact with the sphinx/ext/autodoc/mock.py file (especially the _MockObject class) and the sphinx/util/typing.py functions (restify and stringify). The tests in tests/test_util_typing.py serve as a common integration point.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Feature 1 provides the implementation fix ensuring the internal attributes (__name__ and __qualname__) are correctly set, while Feature 2 adds test cases that validate the fix. The test cases in Feature 2 must be coordinated to reflect the changes made in Feature 1, ensuring that when the implementation is updated, the new tests pass as expected.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers working on the implementation and those writing the tests need to coordinate closely. They should discuss the exact changes to the _MockObject's attributes and confirm that the test scenarios in tests/test_util_typing.py correctly capture the intended behavior. Regular check-ins are advised to ensure consistency and proper integration of the changes across the documentation generation system.
